content:
I was able to scrape together a proof on the fact that regular language is closed under concatenation I used the Mathlib.Computability.EpsilonNFA definition of an NFA and the Mathlib.Computability.DFA
Specifically, the language accepted by M1 concatenated to language accepted by M2 is equal to the language accepted by the the epsilonNFA of both these machines... this isnt exactly using the IsRegular definiton.

I request some feedback on whether this is considered a "good" proof.
Thank you so much for your time.
Brief feedback: the proofs are too long (consider factoring out sublemmas) and you're using nonterminal simps (simp should only be used to close a goal, not to simplify it).
if not using simps should i instead use rewrites? ahh nevermind i got it ,lemmas to make either these simps terminal or be able to use rw instead

You can squeeze non-terminal simps with simp? and then clicking on the blue "apply" in the infoview to change to simp only. But if you care about learning (which you seem to!) then you should look at the output and think to yourself "I typed simp here because I didn't really know what to do, but now I am seeing the actual lemmas which simp used and I could rewrite these directly".

yeah ok ok im working on rewording and making some new lemmas to try and make it work as for simp only is that better than non terminal "simp" but still a clearer terminal "simp" or similarly a terminal "simp at _" is best right?
